name: GE Cync Indoor Smart Plug

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plus Bluetooth LE. The CSA listing gives Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; GE's spec sheet (model CPLGSTDBLW1, no Matter mentioned, so possibly the older version) says the same.

matter.note: CSA lists 'Cync Indoor Plug' by Savant (certificate CSA257FBMAT46925-24, Matter 1.3); other Cync Indoor Plug certificates also exist. Older non-Matter units were sold under the same name.

apple_home.note: Through Matter; needs an Apple home hub.

google_home.note: Native through the Cync app's Google Home link; GE says it can also be added through Matter.

alexa.note: Native through the Cync Alexa skill; GE says it can also be added through Matter.

smartthings.note: GE lists SmartThings for the Matter version; needs a SmartThings Matter controller.

home_assistant.note: There's no official Cync integration in Home Assistant, and neither GE nor Home Assistant names this plug for HA's Matter integration.

hubRequired.note: GE says no hub is required; it connects to Wi-Fi and is set up in the Cync app or a Matter app.

localControl.note: GE's spec sheet lists 'Local Control via BLE', but it doesn't mention Matter and may describe the older version. Local control of the Matter version isn't confirmed.

energyMonitoring.note: GE's pages and spec sheet don't mention power metering, but we found no explicit statement either way.

maxLoadWatts.note: GE's store lists 1800 W / 15 A and the spec sheet says 15 A general use, 1/3 HP, but we couldn't tie a watt figure to the Matter version's own page.

summary: This record covers the Matter version of the GE Cync Indoor Smart Plug, sold in the US. It's a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plug rated 15 A that works with Alexa and Google Home through the Cync app and, through Matter, with Apple Home and SmartThings. No hub is needed.
caveats: Older Cync Indoor Smart Plugs sold under the same name aren't Matter; check the box or listing for 'Matter Compatible'.
Apple Home and SmartThings need a Matter controller, such as an Apple home hub or a SmartThings hub.
If you set it up through Matter and later want to use the Cync app, GE says to reset the plug first.
